'''Klaus Hommels''' (born February 17, 1967) is a German [[venture capitalist]]. He focuses on early and growth-stage investments and has founded his own venture capital fund by the name of Lakestar, through which he has been investing mainly in digital businesses. He has been invested in [[Facebook]], [[Skype Technologies|Skype]] and [[XING|Xing]];<ref>[http://www.spotify.com/en/about/press/spotify-appoints-klaus-hommels-to-board-of-directors/ Spotify appoints Klaus Hommels to Board of Directors] By Spotify Press Release, 21/09/2009, Spotify.com</ref><ref>[http://www.swedishwire.com/business/989-spotify-eyeing-stock-exchange-listing Spotify eyeing stock-exchange listing] The Swedish Wire, 21/09/2009, swedishwire.com</ref> other examples are [[Klarna]] and [[Revolut]].<ref name=":0" />

== Early life and education ==
Hommels graduated with a Master of Science in Business Administration and a PhD in [[Finance]] from the [[University of Fribourg]] (Switzerland).<ref>{{Cite web|title=Klaus Hommels - News & Infos von Business Insider|url=https://www.businessinsider.de/themen/klaus-hommels/|access-date=2022-01-26|website=Business Insider|language=de-DE}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-10-03|title=Klaus Hommels Vermögen|url=https://www.dasvermoegen.com/klaus-hommels-vermoegen/|access-date=2022-01-26|website=Das Vermögen|language=de-DE}}</ref> After graduating, he started working for [[Bertelsmann]] as an [[Secretary|Executive Assistant]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Rinke|first=Florian|date=2019-05-28|title=Lakestar-Gründer Klaus Hommels: Der Mann mit dem Wow-Gespür|trans-title=Lakestar founder Klaus Hommels: The man with the wow-sense|url=https://rp-online.de/nrw/staedte/moenchengladbach/klaus-hommels-aus-juechen-in-den-start-up-olymp_aid-39075923|access-date=2022-01-26|website=RP ONLINE|language=de}}</ref> He was Managing Director for AOL Germany from 1995 to 1999 in the areas of business development, content, and advertising. He then worked for the private equity firm [[Apax Partners]] in [[Munich]] as a director until 2000.

At the height of the [[Dot-com bubble]], he began investing in technology startups as a private investor. During this time, he invested in numerous notable startups. These included companies like Facebook.{{Contradictory inline|date=March 2023|reason=Facebook was founded years after that bubble}} After six years as a private investor, he moved to London in 2006 as a venture partner at [[Benchmark (venture capital firm)|Benchmark Capital]] (now Balderton Capital).<ref>{{Cite web |title=DLD Conference: Digital-Life-Design |url=https://dld-conference.com/speaker/klaus-hommels |access-date=2022-01-26 |website=dld-conference.com}}</ref>

In 2019, Hommels advocated for a sovereign wealth fund in the EU, among other things.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Poschardt |first=Ulf |date=2019-11-16 |title=Investor Klaus Hommels: "Deutschland verliert den Anschluss" |language=de |trans-title=Investor Klaus Hommels: "Germany is losing the connection". |work=DIE WELT |url=https://www.welt.de/wirtschaft/plus203528578/Investor-Klaus-Hommels-Deutschland-verliert-den-Anschluss.html |access-date=2022-01-26}}</ref>

== Investments ==
=== Hommels Holding ===
After a year with Benchmark, he founded Hommels Holding in 2007, resuming his private investing in technology and Internet-based businesses.<ref>[http://www.balderton.com/news-events/klaus-hommels-joins-benchmark-capital-europe-as-venture-partner,,81/ KLAUS HOMMELS JOINS BENCHMARK CAPITAL EUROPE AS VENTURE PARTNER] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100918040657/http://balderton.com/news-events/klaus-hommels-joins-benchmark-capital-europe-as-venture-partner,,81/ |date=September 18, 2010 }} By Benchmark Capital Europe, 05/06/2006, Benchmark press release</ref><ref>[http://insight.iese.edu/doc.aspx?id=722&ar=7/ Klaus Hommels: The Midas King of Entrepreneurs] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110719210949/http://insight.iese.edu/doc.aspx?id=722&ar=7/ |date=July 19, 2011 }} By IESE INSIGHT, 2007</ref> In 2009, it was announced that Hommels had made an investment in the startup, [[Spotify]]. As part of the announcement, he also became a member of its board. He was an early-stage investor in the company, with a valuation of around £20-£30 million.<ref name="gigaom">{{cite web |last1=Andrews |first1=Robert |title=Spotify Reveals Investment From VC Hommels, Adds Him To Board |url=https://gigaom.com/2009/09/21/419-spotify-confirms-investment-from-vc-hommels-adds-him-to-board/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150311013055/https://gigaom.com/2009/09/21/419-spotify-confirms-investment-from-vc-hommels-adds-him-to-board/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=March 11, 2015 |publisher=[[Gigaom]] |date=September 21, 2009}}</ref>

Hommels has invested in several major startups and also had many notable exits. Prior to Lakestar, Hommels was an early investor in many tech startups. One of his first major investments was in the [[Germany|German]]-social media startup, [[XING|Xing]]. According to a [[Business Insider]] report, it was the first social media company to IPO globally.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Gobry |first1=Pascal-Emmanuel |title=Sorry, But LinkedIn Is NOT The First Social Network IPO |url=https://www.businessinsider.com/linkedin-first-ipo-2011-1?r=US&IR=T |publisher=[[Business Insider]] |date=January 27, 2011}}</ref> In 2007, Hommels exited his position with [[QXL.com]], which was sold for £946 million.<ref>{{cite web |last1=White |first1=Dominic |title=Naspers pays £946m for auctioneer QXL |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/finance/markets/2821450/Naspers-pays-946m-for-auctioneer-QXL.html |publisher=[[The Daily Telegraph|The Telegraph]] |date=December 17, 2007}}</ref> He also invested in Spotify in 2009.<ref name="gigaom" /> He also invested in [[Skype]] and exited the position when it was acquired by [[Microsoft]] in May 2011 for $8.5 billion.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Knoke |first1=Felix |title=The Growth of Berlin into Europe's Start-Up Hub |url=http://www.spiegel.de/international/business/raw-and-direct-the-growth-of-berlin-into-europe-s-start-up-hub-a-795949.html |publisher=[[Der Spiegel|Spiegel]]}}</ref>

=== Lakestar ===
Following these initial successes, Hommels founded Lakestar, a [[venture capital]] firm based in Zurich, in 2012.<ref>{{Cite web |title=About |url=https://www.lakestar.com/about |access-date=2022-01-26 |website=Lakestar |language=en |archive-date=January 21, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220121043949/https://www.lakestar.com/about |url-status=dead }}</ref> The company focused on early and growth stage investments, with a priority in [[B2B e-commerce|B2B commerce]], digitization and deep tech, fintech, games and media, healthcare, logistics, as well as travel and mobility. Besides the Zurich office, Lakestar has an international presence in Berlin and London.

Since 2012, Lakestar has developed a good brand name, however as performance of the funds become more clear, its reputation has been questioned. There has been several articles on [https://www.handelsblatt.com/technik/it-internet/militaertechnologie-investor-klaus-hommels-wird-aufsichtsratschef-beim-nato-innovationsfonds/29048526.html Klaus Hommels] on Handelsblatt. The venture capital firm's first fund decided to extend the fund life by a year in 2023.<ref>{{cite web|access-date=2022-01-25|author=James Cook|language=en-US|title=European investor Klaus Hommels is launching a new €350 million fund — we talked to him about the Silicon Valley of Europe and whether we're in a tech bubble|url=https://www.businessinsider.com/klaus-hommels-interview-about-lakestar-second-fund-launch-2015-8|website=businessinsider.com}}<!-- auto-translated by Module:CS1 translator --></ref><ref>{{cite web|access-date=2022-01-25|date=2021-11-02|language=de-DE|title=Jack Ma Family Office investiert in $735M Lakestar Fonds|url=https://www.listenchampion.de/2021/11/02/jack-ma-family-office-investiert-in-735m-lakestar-fonds/|website=Listenchampion}}<!-- auto-translated by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> In 2013, Lakestar announced the launch of its first institutional fund, Lakestar I, with a total size of €150 million. Lakestar I subsequently invested in several European startups<ref>{{cite web|last1=Cook|first1=James|date=August 23, 2015|title=European investor Klaus Hommels is launching a new €350 million fund|url=https://www.businessinsider.com/klaus-hommels-interview-about-lakestar-second-fund-launch-2015-8?IR=T|publisher=[[Business Insider]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last1=Lomas|first1=Natasha|date=January 23, 2014|title=GoEuro Gets "Multi-Million" Top-Up From Lakestar To Add More Markets To Its Journey Planner Platform|url=https://techcrunch.com/2014/01/23/goeuro-post-seed/|publisher=[[TechCrunch]]}}</ref> and participated in a $27 million funding round for [[Omio]], formerly GoEuro, among other investments.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Coleman|first1=Alison|date=August 27, 2014|title=German Startup GoEuro Closes $27M Funding Round, While Berlin Closes In On London As Europe's Investment Capital|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/alisoncoleman/2014/08/27/german-start-up-goeuro-closes-27-million-funding-round-while-berlin-closes-in-on-london-as-europes-investment-capital/#4dd8377c5b11|work=[[Forbes]]}}</ref> In 2019, Lakestar's most recent fund raised $700 million.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Ghost |first1=Shona |title=Raising Europe's Biggest startup Fund |url=https://www.businessinsider.com/inside-lakestar-800-million-venture-capital-startup-fundraise-2019-06 |publisher=[[Business Insider]] }}{{Dead link|date=March 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Finanzierung Fuer Innovationen Investor Klaus Hommels Legt 700 Millionen-Dollar Fonds Fuer Start-ups |trans-title=Financing For Innovations Investor Klaus Hommels Launches 700 Million-Dollar Fund For Start-ups |url=https://www.handelsblatt.com/finanzen/anlagestrategie/fonds-etf/finanzierung-fuer-innovationen-investor-klaus-hommels-legt-700-millionen-dollar-fonds-fuer-start-ups-auf/25058564.html?ticket=ST-6692038-kaAyIUgXeNMCn6OcoNlH-ap2 |publisher=Handelsblatt}}</ref> Other investments of Lakestar include Sennder, Glovo, [[GetYourGuide]], for example.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Levingston |first1=Ivan |title=Revolut and Spotify investor to stop raising outside funds |url=https://www.ft.com/content/f1e23f0e-dd5d-431a-abb7-21bc635f7a2a |access-date=23 October 2025 |work=Financial Times |date=23 October 2025}}</ref>

In 2021, Hommels/Lakestar was the first European venture capital fund to sponsor a special purpose investment vehicle (SPAC) totaling $332 million.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Browne|first=Ryan|date=2021-02-17|title=Tech investor Klaus Hommels launches $332 million SPAC in Europe|url=https://www.cnbc.com/2021/02/17/lakestar-founder-klaus-hommels-launches-europes-first-tech-spac.html|access-date=2021-02-19|website=CNBC|language=en}}</ref>

== Other activities ==
* since 2016: Internet Economy Foundation (IE.F), Member of the Board<ref>{{cite web |title=Avec Juke, Juniper veut s'imposer dans le multi-cloud |url=https://www.zdnet.fr/actualites/avec-juke-juniper-veut-s-imposer-dans-le-multi-cloud-39887521.htm |publisher=[[ZDNet]]}}</ref>
* since 2021: [[Munich Security Conference]] (MSC), Member of the Security Innovation Board<ref>{{Cite web|title=Security Innovation Board|url=https://securityconference.org/en/about-us/security-innovation-board/|access-date=2022-01-26|website=securityconference.org|language=en}}</ref>
* 2021/2022: Vice-[[Chairperson|Chair]] and Chair-elect of Invest Europe, an industry association representing investment firms

Hommels is a member of the advisory and supervisory boards of various companies, including Revolut, Sennder and Isar Aerospace. He actively advocates for the digital sovereignty of Europe, supporting the ''Scale Up'' initiative of [[Emmanuel Macron]], for example.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Martin-Jung |first=Helmut |title=Deutschland fehlen zwei Billionen Euro |url=https://www.sueddeutsche.de/wirtschaft/hommels-spotify-skype-zalando-innovation-1.5506832 |access-date=2022-06-14 |website=Süddeutsche.de |language=de}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Interview: Wagnisfinanzierer Klaus Hommels: "Wir brauchen digitale Souveränität" |url=https://www.handelsblatt.com/finanzen/banken-versicherungen/banken/interview-wagnisfinanzierer-klaus-hommels-wir-brauchen-digitale-souveraenitaet/26848324.html |access-date=2022-06-14 |website=www.handelsblatt.com |language=de}}</ref>

== Honors ==
In 2006, Hommels was named Europe's most successful entrepreneurial private investor by leading European business schools [[IESE]], [[INSEAD]], and the [[University of St. Gallen]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Giving ideas wings |newspaper=[[The Economist]] |date=14 September 2006 }}</ref>

In 2017, Hommels ranked third by [[Forbes]] on its first-ever Midas Touch list.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Konrad |first1=Alex |title=How Midas List Investor Klaus Hommels Became Europe's Startup Secret Weapon |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/alexkonrad/2017/11/06/klaus-hommels-europe-startup-secret-weapon/#2ef31d74583a |work=[[Forbes]]}}</ref> In 2019, Hommels was ranked 46th on the global Midas list and 5th on the European Midas list by Forbes.<ref>{{cite web |title=Top Companies Behind the Midas List Europe 2019 |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/truebridge/2019/12/02/top-companies-behind-the-midas-list-europe-2019/#451607375d9e |work=[[Forbes]] |date=December 2, 2019}}</ref> In 2021, he is ranked 6th on the ''European Top Tech Investors'' list and 31st on the global ''Top Tech Investors'' list.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Klaus Hommels|url=https://www.forbes.com/profile/klaus-hommels/|access-date=2022-01-26|website=forbes.com|language=en}}</ref> In 2022, Hommels was also on the Midas List, mentioning his investment in Revolut.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Midas List 2022 |url=https://www.forbes.com/midas/ |access-date=2022-05-04 |website=Forbes}}</ref>
